items.notes: Manual semantic review binds Cook4Me 'Liquid caramel' to USDA FNDDS 'Caramel dip, regular'. The target describes caramel in a pourable/liquid form, and the target's own pinned evidence contains this regular caramel-dip record. A dip is a closer physical and nutritional proxy for liquid caramel than solid caramel candy. Confidence remains medium because the source does not specify water, sugar, dairy, butter, syrup concentration, or whether this is a dessert topping versus cooking caramel; this review does not generalize to filled candies or caramel-coated foods.

Manual semantic review binds Cook4Me 'Rose syrup' to USDA FNDDS 'Simple syrup'. Rose syrup is fundamentally a sugar syrup flavored with rose, and the target's own pinned evidence ranks simple syrup first. Confidence remains medium because rose aroma/extract, color, exact sugar concentration, and possible additives are not represented separately; this review does not generalize to rose wine, fruit syrups, or reduced-sugar flavored drinks.

Manual semantic review binds Cook4Me 'Pickled onions' to USDA SR Legacy 'Onions, raw'. The target is unambiguously onion and its own pinned evidence ranks the raw onion record first, so this is used as a same-food proxy while preserving onion identity. Confidence remains medium because pickling changes sodium, acidity, sugar, water balance, and sometimes onion variety; those brine effects are not represented and this review does not generalize to relishes, chutneys, or cooked onion dishes.

Manual semantic review binds Cook4Me 'Qamar al-din apricot juice' to USDA FNDDS 'Apricot nectar*. Qamar al-din is an apricot-based drink prepared from concentrated/dried apricot material and water, and the target's own pinned evidence contains apricot nectar as the closest apricot beverage record. Confidence remains medium because the exact dilution, added sugar, apricot solids, and preparation from apricot leather are not represented; this review does not generalize to raw apricot, mixed orange-apricot drinks, or apricot kernel products.

Manual semantic review binds Cook4Me 'Sliced scamorza cheese' to USDA Foundation 'Cheese, provolone, sliced'. Scamorza and provolone are both cow-milk pasta-filata cheeses, and the target's own pinned evidence ranks sliced provolone first while also matching the sliced form. Confidence remains medium because scamorza has its own moisture, aging, and possible smoking profile that is not represented by provolone; this review does not imply identical cheese subtype or generalize to cream cheese, cheddar, or imitation cheese.

Manual semantic review binds Cook4Me 'Vanilla flavouring' to USDA SR Legacy 'Vanilla extract'. Vanilla extract is the target's own top-ranked pinned evidence and represents the common liquid vanilla flavoring used in recipes. Confidence remains medium because the catalog wording does not distinguish natural extract from artificial vanilla flavor, vanilla paste, powder, or alcohol-free formulations; this review does not generalize to vanilla-flavored dairy or desserts.
